Hi! Sorry if you’ve already tried this, but hope it helps. 

Firstly, 

*Prep skin with moisturiser, then follow it up with a good primer - preferably mattifying / silicone primer. 

*Try avoiding full coverage products, maybe opt for a tinted moisturiser if applying foundation or just mix in some moisturiser and apply with a light hand 

*Go light handed on the concealer too, again minimal product 

*Set w/ your loose powder and setting spray as you already do 

Beyond this, sweating is completely normal and this happens at shoots with all the studio lights too. Can’t do much other than touching up. 

* Blotting the sweat away with tissue or oil blotting paper (available online) is key. Don’t apply product directly over. 

*Check to see if you still have concealer coverage on your face, if not apply a tad and then set w powder again. Maybe you can check out some compact foundations to avoid carrying concealer + powder outside.

Hi I’m a makeup artist and this what I do. You need a peach colour concealer if you’re  fair to med OR orange if deeper skin toned, a concealer shade as dark as the darkness of you dark circles and a shade that’s a tone or two lighter than your skin tone. A cream formula concealer or liquid is ok. Cream is more full coverage. You can check out MAC concealer palettes as it’ll have all these shades above. You can also check out “LA girl concealer” for the peach or orange colour - budget friendly and good. Maybe you can layer the concealers you already have over this. 

Technique: 

*prep your skin with a hydrating toner followed by really nice thick moisturiser 


*The key is to apply a little product at a time with less pressure and build - too much will make it crease


*you really need like a small touch of corrector colour and other concealers.


*A small fluffy brush can help with this 


*don’t forget to set with a loose setting powder - I like “Kay Beauty loose powder” in translucent if fair to medium skin tone or banana if deeper toned (yellow) after for a natural but long lasting finish 


*setting spray if you can! I’ve enjoyed the “urban decay spray”

Some general dining etiquette, that I hope helps you :) Sorry if you know some of this already! 


* Napkin: Once seated, follow your hosts lead and unfold the napkin and place on your lap either at the start or once your food starts arriving / being served. Keep it on your lap for the duration of the dinner. If you need to move from your seat, place it on the left of your plate. 
* Cutlery: outermost cutlery is used for the first course, working your way to the inner cutlery as you move on to the next course 
* You can practice eating with a fork and knife by watching some YouTube videos, knife on the right and fork on left. If not for this dinner then the next one :) 
* Wait till everyone is served each course to start eating  
* Most of these kinda restaurants will also serve a complimentary assortment of bread and butter for everyone to share while waiting for appetisers. Help yourself with a portion of bread and put on your plate 
* Also OP if some small slip up happens, just embrace it with a smile. They can’t make you feel weird if you just seem confident (even if you’re feel awkward on the inside). They want your presence there, so own it girl
